purpose: Reusable information architecture and diagram grammar extracted from 19 AIA reference pages; not a visual brand/style profile.

provenance.review_status: provisional GPT-6 visual expert pass; independent human adjudication pending

patterns.use_when: Compare two market indicators or several providers over a shared time range.
rules: Use shared time scale where comparable.
Label units and source per chart.
Add one conclusion band outside plot area.
Avoid too many series; highlight focal series.

patterns.use_when: Explain market/product mix and connect it to product or balance-sheet detail.
rules: Use pie/donut only for a small number of mutually exclusive parts.
Pair with table only when table answers a distinct follow-up question.
Keep labels and legend readable; avoid duplicating percentages.

patterns.use_when: Show a central capability/persona surrounded by 5–7 related dimensions.
rules: Center label names the organizing concept.
Each spoke should be parallel in grammar and length.
Keep explanatory copy outside the radial icon ring.

patterns.use_when: Break a total into branches, drivers and explanatory factors.
rules: Root is the outcome/total.
Branches represent mutually distinguishable drivers.
Leaf text explains mechanism, not restates category.

patterns.use_when: Explain population tiers, service tiers or capability maturity.
rules: Define the dimension that determines tier placement.
Keep each tier concise and labels aligned.
Place detailed evidence in a side column or next page.

patterns.use_when: Explain sequential actions, online-offline handoffs or conversion.
rules: Use one unambiguous direction.
Distinguish stages from feedback loops.
Label handoff and outcome explicitly.
Do not overload nodes with paragraphs.

patterns.use_when: Pair a human or social context image with a time-series or quantitative proof.
rules: Image establishes context, not decoration.
Chart must independently support the claim.
Use one concise takeaway to connect emotional and analytical evidence.

patterns.use_when: Classify segments using two or three explicit dimensions.
rules: Prefer 2D matrix when axes are categorical.
If 3D perspective is used, label all axes and explain how cells map to categories.
Avoid perspective depth as a substitute for clear relationship encoding.

anti_patterns: tables with footnotes colliding with final rows
long explanatory paragraphs inside pyramid tiers
multiple independent claims competing on one page
style_transfer_policy: Do not copy AIA beige/gold palette, logo, typography or decorative language into GCL style. Transfer only semantic structure and diagram grammar.
